Customs Act 1969: Section 19 of this Act empowers the Government to grant exemptions from import duties and other taxes.
The First Schedule of this Act is referenced to identify specific goods subject to customs regulation and potential exemption.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(1) of this Act provides the legal authority for the Government to grant exemptions from value added tax in the public interest.
National Board of Revenue: The Government exercises its exemption powers in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
S.R.O. 88-AIN/2010: This previous notification is formally repealed by the current regulatory order.
First Schedule: The goods listed in the table are identified based on their Heading Numbers and H.S. Codes as defined in the First Schedule of the Customs Act.
H.S. Code: Specific commodities ranging from agricultural produce to industrial minerals are classified under these codes for the purpose of granting tax and duty exemptions.
Standard Rules of Origin 1977: Goods qualify for duty and tax exemptions only if they meet the conditions specified in these rules regarding their origin.
Goods: A specified list of agricultural products, fruits, minerals, and industrial raw materials originating from Bhutan are exempted from import duty, value added tax, supplementary duty, and regulatory duty.
